articles.title: ‘Strong togetherness’: Slegers feels support from Arsenal hierarchy despite miserable run
articles.summary: Board ‘really good and positive’ at ‘difficult time’ Gunners visit WSL leaders Manchester City on Sunday. Renée Slegers says she has felt the full support of Arsenal’s board and praised her senior players for showing “monumental leadership” this week as she vows to find solutions to recent poor…
body: One win in five matches has left Slegers under mounting pressure. Arsenal let slip a two-goal lead to draw at Paris FC in the Women’s Champions League on Wednesday and in the WSL they have slipped seven points behind City, the leaders and defending champions, having scored once in their past three league games.

Slegers was in a determined mood on Friday, speaking of a “strong togetherness” at the club. Asked whether she felt the full support of the board, she replied: “Yes, that’s what I felt. That’s been positive and that’s helped me. The club’s leadership has been really good and positive for me in this moment because everyone thinks this is a difficult time and this is not something that we want for the team and for the club.

“But the leadership from Clare [Wheatley, the director of football], Rich [Garlick, CEO], James [King, director of football operations], Jodie [Taylor, techical director] has been superb. So I want to give everything back to the club.

Whereas the Super League era has traditionally been dominated by the powerhouses of the sport with their heaving trophy cabinets, 2026 is the story of one side that has come close but not got over the line and another that has upset the odds to wedge themselves into the conversation.

articles.title: Mercedes put team first as Russell and Antonelli face off on F1’s return to Sepang
articles.summary: Title rivals bring upgrades to first Grand Prix in Malaysia since 2017 on a demanding but well liked circuit. While the byzantine nomenclature of this weekend’s “Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia” will have Formula One’s statisticians muttering darkly under their breath for years to come, the import…
body: The return to Malaysia for its first race since 2017 has been welcomed in F1. It is a much-liked circuit among drivers, albeit the high temperatures and humidity make for an enormous physical challenge.

However, this is no long-term return to Sepang. It is back, as its torturously titled branding suggests, as a one-off replacement for the Bahrain GP, which was cancelled earlier this year because of the war in the Middle East. The Bahrain GP it is then, right down to the Bahraini backing, a Bahrain GP trophy and Bahraini-themed activities at the circuit but the pole and the victory will most assuredly be earned in Sepang, leading to said statisticians deploying the asterisk on their keyboard.

For the title protagonists, however, the name is moot. What matters is the race and both the championship leader, Kimi Antonelli, and his rival and Mercedes teammate George Russell want to make a mark in Malaysia. Antonelli leads Russell by 66 points with eight rounds remaining. A handsome lead but he dropped 15 points to the British driver at the last round in Baku where Russell showed the best form of his season, dominant across the weekend.

articles.summary: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Seven days after leaking out, the Manchester City saga has become a flood. Peace in our time has disappeared into the distance as football jurisprudence’s longest-running case enters Defcon 1 lawfare.
body: In the absence of a more august body tackling the issue, may I be so bold as to suggest both an expansion, and a revision of the much missed Gareth Bale Scale, given the state of our long-ago once ‘beautiful game’ (and an overlong international break). Thus: Infantino, Manchester City, Southampton, VAR, Argentina. In this topsy-turvy world, top, is of course bottom, or thereabouts” – Michael Lloyd.

I am struggling to think of any other jurisprudence where the true victims of the crime (the fans) are also the victims of the punishment. As Spanish Football Daily would say, siempre pagan justos por pecadores” – Mark Brookes.

Having nothing better to do this evening, I knocked up a little Python program to replay the results of several ‘tainted’ seasons, to see what effect might be had from removing Manchester City’s results. I got a hit for 2010-11 where Blackpool, who finished second from bottom and were relegated, would have actually come fourth from bottom had there been no City games. Look, I know it doesn’t really make any sense, my doing this, but still intriguing” – John Guthrie.

articles.title: Tankards, Clough & 'creaky joints' - Tennent's Sixes returns
articles.summary: More than three decades since its last staging, Scottish football's cult indoor event makes a comeback with the "creaky joints" of former players taking to an ice rink.
body: There really was a time when Scottish football's top players would be signed off for a weekend to represent their clubs in a mid-season six-a-side tournament.

Now, 33 years on from its previous iteration, the "creaky joints" of the Scottish game, as Rangers hero Ian Durrant puts it, will hobble about on an artificial surface rolled out over Braehead Arena's ice rink.

The cult indoor event returns this weekend, with former players representing each of Scotland's 12 top-flight sides. They will play group-stage matches on Saturday before a new winner is decided on Sunday evening.
With the assistance of Durrant, Barry Ferguson will manage a Rangers team including the likes of Charlie Adam and Andy Halliday, while Aiden McGeady and Charlie Mulgrew are among Celtic's squad.

articles.title: Timely recognition or long overdue? How Gross is proving all-time bargain
articles.summary: Named the Premier League's player of the month for September, BBC Sport looks at Brighton star Pascal Gross' impact both this season and over the past nine years during his two spells at the club.
body: Having been named the top-flight's player of the month for September, it leads to the question of whether Brighton midfielder Pascal Gross may be one of the best value-for-money signings in Premier League history.
In fact the 35-year-old has effectively cost the Seagulls minus £3m - and been involved in 85 Premier League goals over two spells.
Nobody has been involved in more top-flight goals than Gross this season - six in five games.
He was Brighton 's first Premier League signing in 2017 for a reported £3m from Ingolstadt and left for his boyhood club Borussia Dortmund in 2024 for £8m.

articles.title: Mariota to start for Commanders in London as Daniels ruled out
articles.summary: Washington Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota will get his second start in place of the injured Jayden Daniels on Sunday when his side face the Indianapolis Colts at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
body: Head coach Dan Quinn announced the decision on Friday after practice at the team's hotel accommodations outside London.

Daniels returned to practice this week after dislocating his elbow in Week Two against the Dallas Cowboys. He's been wearing a protective brace and had expressed no concerns about further damage, but the Commanders will hold him out for at least one more game.
"[Daniels] had a great week. It was awesome to have him back on the field in a limited fashion," Quinn said. "He'll be out. Marcus will start."
Quinn called Daniels' return to practice "a huge positive step for him and for us."

articles.title: Update on Mason Graham’s knee injury for Browns
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns DT Mason Graham was off to a tremendous start to his second season, notching four sacks in his first three games. Then came yesterday’s game against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football.
body: The bad news is that Graham will miss some time, but the good news is that it does not appear to be a long-term injury. Rapoport says that Graham suffered an MCL sprain and an ankle sprain when his leg bent backwards, injuries which should keep him out for a few weeks.

Let’s say he misses the rest of October, which would be three games — those would come against the New York Jets, Baltimore Ravens, and Tennessee Titans. Then, on November 1, Cleveland takes on the Steelers again. We’ll see how things go with Graham week-by-week, but if the Browns keep playing the way they are, they could have a solid record by the time he gets back. It’s possible that the Browns place Graham on the short-term IR list too, which would open up a roster spot in exchange for him missing four games.
The Browns will rely on Maliek Collins, Mike Hall Jr, and Adin Huntington at defensive tackle. I would expect them to also call up Sam Kamara from the practice squad soon.

articles.title: Who is Rui Pinto? The whistleblower abandoned by Portuguese authorities over Man City leaks
articles.summary: Manchester City find themselves at the centre of the biggest story in Premier League history as they face potential relegation or expulsion from a division they currently lead, after being found guilty of nearly all of the 115 charges levied against them. But this scandal had humble beginnings.
body: Rui Pinto is the Portuguese hacker who blew the whistle on City’s financial cheating, prompting an entire Premier League investigation.

Through his website Football Leaks, he published confidential documents that showed City broke league rules over a nine-season period in 2018. German newspaper Der Spiegel ’s subsequent investigative report detailing allegations against City was based on these documents.

Pinto was in other legal trouble by the time the City allegations took the football world by storm. After being unmasked as the man behind Football Leaks, he faced 147 charges that included computer fraud, attempted extortion and violating privacy of correspondence in Portugal, having published a number of stories about other players and clubs including those relating to Porto and Benfica. He was extradited from Hungary, where he had been living, in March 2019.

articles.title: England bowler Carse charged by Cricket Regulator over nightclub incident
articles.summary: Brydon Carse has been charged by the Cricket Regulator in relation to events in Derby in August where he was ‌handcuffed by police and then dropped from the England squad.
body: Footage emerged on social media of Carse in handcuffs, having been arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly in the early hours of Sunday August 23.
The 31-year-old was celebrating with Durham players after their win at Derbyshire in the County Championship.

He was dropped from England's Test squad for the rest of their series with Pakistan, after which Derbyshire Police confirmed it was looking into allegations of assault but they ended their investigation last month.
Carse was later omitted from the T20I and ODI squads for the ongoing series against Sri Lanka.

articles.summary: Expert racing pundit Kevin Blake will be in Paris for the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe and picks out three fancies on the undercard, all live on Sky Sports Racing.
body: Qatar Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe weekend at ParisLongchamp, live on Sky Sports Racing, is without doubt one of the crown jewels in the world of horse racing.
The feature race at 3.05pm on Sunday is one of the most prestigious races in the sport and the supporting card is dripping with Group 1 races.
With unusually dry weather having prevailed in recent weeks, the racing looks likely to take place on what we would call good ground if not a little firmer.

Sunday's renewal of the Prix de l'Abbaye de Longchamp Longines (1:47) is perhaps one of the weaker ones in recent years, but one factor that always persists in it is the importance of the draw. A low draw is a significant advantage and for that reason I am favouring the Francis-Henri Graffard-trained SHIRI, who is drawn in stall four.
